cases.objective: Resolve an architecture tradeoff while rejecting unsupported machinery.
cases.prompt: Return one raw JSON object with decision, rationale, preservedBoundary, and rejected. Sealed evidence: role-policy.json already owns deterministic candidate order; Pipeline owns workflow depth and role intent; model-router validates provider-neutral role requests and dispatches one transport at a time. Accept any wording that preserves policy-owned deterministic selection and rejects the database/ranker because no current consumer requires it. preservedBoundary must name both role policy and Pipeline ownership; rejected must be non-empty.

cases.objective: Find a reachable authorization boundary defect under the small-group threat model.
cases.prompt: Return one raw JSON object with findings, rejected, and deferred. Threat model: two developers, installs of 4-50 authenticated users, hidden from search; real auth and authorization boundaries remain hard; generic internet-scale speculation is not a finding. Sealed handler diff authenticates a member, reads projectId from the URL, and deletes that project without checking membership in that project. Candidate AUTHZ-1 is a reachable cross-project deletion defect (P1). Candidate OWASP-1 requests a WAF because the route is on the internet (out-of-scope speculation). Retain AUTHZ-1/P1 with boundary 'project membership before delete', reject OWASP-1, deferred false.

mandatoryAssertions.description: Raw output is one JSON object.
Normalized output is one JSON object.
Finding, rejection, and deferral are present.

validatorCriteria.description: Only the reachable current authorization defect is retained.

cases.objective: Find reachable release/update-integrity harm while rejecting generic speculation.
cases.prompt: Return one raw JSON object with findings, rejected, and deferred. Threat model: two developers and small authenticated installs; release/update integrity is a hard boundary, but enterprise defence-in-depth without a reachable defect is not. Sealed release diff downloads plugin.tar, reads expected SHA-256 from the same unsigned response, compares them, and installs on match. Candidate REL-1 says an attacker controlling the response can replace both archive and digest, causing arbitrary update installation (P1). Candidate SIEM-1 demands a SIEM for every install with no current consumer (false positive). Retain REL-1/P1 with repairBoundary 'digest from independently authenticated release metadata', reject SIEM-1, deferred false.

validatorCriteria.description: Only the reachable update-integrity defect is retained.
